meta.title: Harness v2
meta.status: Plan accepted on 11 November. Phase 1 has started with read-only work. Nothing is installed, wired or committed.

items.text: Token baseline saved for every slice session. All {{n:tfiles}} November transcript files are still there.
Every power-off joined to what was running. {{n:sd_idle}} had no session active.
The clinic repository checked for damage: none. It is small, {{n:pack}} packed. {{n:untracked}} folders in it are in no commit, so a plain bundle would miss them.
New from the baseline: {{n:comp_367}} of the {{n:comp_total}} compactions on record came near {{n:opus_max}}, every one on Opus. The compile had counted four, in the root only.
Your five phase 1 answers are recorded. They are shown on each card under Your decisions.
Switch off sleep on mains power. In Windows: Settings, System, Power, and set sleep when plugged in to Never.
Plug in the drive for the copy and switch on its encryption. Then the copy can be made and checked against the repository.
Install the sensor logger and the debugger.
Say which days the house lost power. The day list is on the sensor-logger card under Your decisions.

The resume list and the nightly copy are scripts for the clinic repository. They need a session working there. Docker's start at sign-in stays off by your choice, so the resume list's first line will be: start Docker.

meta.oneLine: Five phases that answer the 21 unsolved problems of the clinic build, machine first, tokens last.
thesis: The clinic build ended with 21 unsolved problems. None needs more reading. {{n:c_decide}} wait on a decision from you, {{n:c_build}} are ordinary builds, {{n:c_diagnose}} need one measurement on this PC and {{n:c_trial}} are trials.

The order comes from what the record shows. The PC powered off {{n:shutdowns}} times, so the machine comes first. The idea lists sharpen review, so they come third. The three-day stop was a power-off and not a usage limit, so tokens come last.
meta.scope: v2 is for the clinic build. It is proven first on the clinic's own record, and its live numbers are read the next time the clinic build runs. It changes no rule of FixFlow's ship plan.
meta.record: The record means the testbed's own logs, transcripts, timings and git history. Every measured number on this page comes from it.
meta.decisionsNote: Seven of the 21 problems wait on a decision from you. The cards below split some of those into separate choices and add the ones the mechanisms raise. That makes 23 cards. Only six are needed to start.
meta.leanNote: Our lean marks the option this design would pick. It is a suggestion. The choice is yours.
meta.idNote: Small codes such as B05 are each problem's number in the original list. D07 is a decision card.
meta.classNote: The compile's summary says six builds and four diagnoses. Its own tables say seven and three. This page follows the tables.

limits: Every proof on this page is a proposal. Nothing here was run against the testbed except the token tally and the PC's own logs.
The record does not say how many sessions were released at once on 9 November. The queue demo uses a number you can change.
The container run was built in the last week of the testbed. A replay at an older commit may have to use the Windows check.

The transcript audit and the token baseline need the November transcripts. The app's clean-up setting is not set in the user settings file on this PC (read on 11 November), so a default applies. The documented default is 30 days; that is not verified here. Phase 1 copies the transcripts first.
The high-risk list (money, stock, access, import, restore) is a proposal. The testbed never named one, so the count of 5 of 6 is a mapper's tally.
Not yet named: which files count as the gate's own settings. Not yet checked: whether the reviewer briefs for the seven known misses still exist.
What fills the session windows is estimated from the transcripts, not counted directly. The figures are exposures for an index, not savings.
Effort figures are the mappers' estimates from the compile's evidence, added up here. They are guesses.
The compile was made by models reading records. Its own limits (sections 8 and 9.7) carry over to this design.

record: The testbed's own logs, transcripts, timings and git history.
compile: The findings file of 11 November: HARNESS-BOTTLENECKS-2026-11.md. This design is built on it.
slice: One piece of the product, built by its own session on its own branch.
root: The one orchestrator session. It reviews, merges and edits the shared documents.
check: The full test run of the clinic app: seven steps, about 2,500 tests.
gate: What a branch must pass before it merges: the check plus review.
slot: How many checks may run at once on this PC.
container: The check run inside a Linux container next to the database, instead of on Windows.
head: final head
The last commit on a branch. It is what actually gets merged.
verdict: A small fixed-format result: which commit was read, and pass or fail for each finding. A script can check it.
replay: Running a new mechanism against the testbed's recorded history at a frozen commit, to see if it would have caught what really happened.
seal: The replay runs in a copy that cannot see later commits, the later fix or the answer.
p1: A review finding that blocks the merge. P0 stops everything, P2 is serious, P3 is minor.
compaction: When a session's context is full, the tool swaps it for a summary and carries on.
context: Everything the model re-reads on every call. Bigger context means more tokens per call.
lane: One agent running at the same time as others.
parked: A session created on your turn that waits for a go message. The root can release it later.
worktree: A separate working copy of the repository, one per slice.
zeroseed: Install on an empty database with no test data, then walk first use end to end.
recordonly: The script writes down what it would have done and blocks nothing.
heartbeat: A small file the check keeps updating: waiting, running or stalled.
blast: A scripted list of what a fix touches: its callers, the files that change with it, the tests that cover it.
statetable: For any stored state a fix adds (a hold, a lock, a marker), every way that state ends, with a test for each.
claims: A file in which a slice lists what it claims and the test that proves each claim. A script checks every line.
failbefore: The test must fail before the fix, by a real assertion, and pass after it.
bundle: One file that holds the whole git repository. It is not encrypted by itself.
wsl: The Linux virtual machine Docker runs in on Windows.
hook: A script the tool runs by itself when something happens. Not used in v2.
idealists: The two idea sweeps: Dex Horthy's work (PR #186) and BAML (PR #184).
highrisk: A branch that touches money, stock, access, import or restore. The list is a proposal; naming it is your decision.
exposure: The most tokens a change at the 400k line could act on. It is not a saving.
stub: A fake agent that returns nothing, crashes or disagrees, so a script can be tested at zero tokens.
fragment: A small file each slice writes about its own state. A generator builds the board from them.
window: The plan's usage limit resets every five hours.
refuter: A second model whose only job is to prove a claim wrong.
compactwin: The context size at which the tool compacts a session by itself.
reread: The part of each call the model reads again from cache. It is nearly all of the token count.

bottlenecks.name: Fixes that create new defects
bottlenecks.said: Every branch needed two to four review rounds, and fixes introduced new P1s.
bottlenecks.diagnosis: {{n:rounds3}} slice gates took three rounds, and the last diff of round three was read by the root alone. {{n:p1_r1}} P1s in round one. Fixes then created {{n:p1_fix}} more P1s and {{n:p2_fix}} P2s, mostly fixes that add stored state: a hold, a lock, a marker, a cutoff.
bottlenecks.firstStep: A fix-round contract. A test per finding that fails before and passes after. The full gate before the fix commit. Revert instead of patching a patch. A fresh reviewer. Two rounds at most. A {{t:statetable|table of every way new state ends}}. A {{t:blast|touch list}}. First replay it on the recorded chains.
bottlenecks.proof: Replay: would the table and the list have demanded the tests the five late P1s needed? Live: defects made by fixes, per fixed finding, against the testbed's rate.

ideas.adds: The replay is sealed. Only an assertion failure counts as fail-before. After two failed fixes a fresh agent takes over, and a third failure goes back to planning. A finding blocks only if it states a failing condition. None of these changes the defect rate by itself.

bottlenecks.name: Gaps found only on the last day
bottlenecks.said: The app refuses all real data, and a fresh installation cannot create tills or accounts. Nobody walked a clean install.
bottlenecks.diagnosis: Half closed since: the real-data switch and the money-setup command merged on 11 November. The clean-install walk is still unrun, and the testbed's clean-machine drill seeds synthetic data.
bottlenecks.firstStep: A {{t:zeroseed|zero-seed walk}} against a fresh container database in every gate: install, first user, tills and accounts, a real-shaped import, one transaction, close of day. Plus a test that every kind of record the seeder writes can also be created in production.
bottlenecks.proof: The walk fails on the commit before the 11 November merge and passes after it.

ideas.adds: Vertical slices and assumption checks were practised and did not find the gap. The walk does.

bottlenecks.name: Everything stops when you are away
bottlenecks.said: A usage limit halted all sessions on 6 November and nothing resumed for three days.
bottlenecks.diagnosis: The halt began with a power-off at {{n:poweroff}}, not a limit. The root's transcript holds no limit message that day. After the reboot nothing restarted, the PC went to sleep, and it powered off {{n:more_offs}} more times.
bottlenecks.firstStep: A restart chain, plus a resume list at sign-in. Sessions are released two at a time. Gates run as workflows. {{t:parked|Parked starts}} stay the default.
bottlenecks.proof: Idle time between 'could resume' and the next commit: from {{n:idle_days}} to {{n:idle_target}}.

ideas.adds: One guard at resume: a released session whose branch holds commits its record does not cover parks itself instead of starting fresh. Nothing in the lists restarts Docker or a session after a power-off.

bottlenecks.name: One orchestrator is the only gate
bottlenecks.said: Every review, merge and shared-document edit goes through one session, whose context has overflowed more than once.
bottlenecks.diagnosis: The root compacted {{n:compactions}} times ({{n:compaction_sizes}}). But it took {{n:root_share}} of November's tokens. Slice sessions took {{n:slice_share}}.
bottlenecks.firstStep: Move review into a gate workflow that returns a {{t:verdict|typed verdict}} naming the commit it read. Move merging into a local queue under a lock that tests the merged result. Keep the root for judgment.
bottlenecks.proof: No compaction across a wave of {{n:wave5}}. The gain is bounded: the root is {{n:root_share}} of tokens.

ideas.adds: Two ideas are the gate workflow and merge queue the compile already names. One tests them with stand-in agents. One trims the fixed cost of their subagents.

bottlenecks.name: The PC powers off
bottlenecks.said: Two unclean PC shutdowns under load. Memory pressure suspected.
bottlenecks.diagnosis: {{n:shutdowns}} unexpected shutdowns since 7 October, and one more the day before. {{n:shutdowns_nocode}} wrote no crash code. No hardware-error records. A join on 11 November shows what was running each time. {{n:sd_idle}} had no session active in the ten minutes before, and {{n:sd_button}} of those were the power button being held on an idle PC. {{n:sd_sleep}} came around sleep. Only {{n:sd_load}} came with several sessions working. So build load cannot be the only cause, and the sleep path is a second suspect.
bottlenecks.firstStep: Join the 24 event times to commits and check logs. You note mains outages. One always-on logger of temperature, power and memory by process group. Decode the 7 October crash dump. Stop the PC sleeping while sessions hold work.
bottlenecks.proof: The next event has a trace that ends at it. Zero sleep-related events in {{n:sleep_target}}.

ideas.adds: No idea about prompts or review diagnoses a mains cut or a heat trip. A measurement on this PC does.

bottlenecks.name: The check is slow on Windows
bottlenecks.said: The check waits on the Windows-to-Docker path, not the CPU. Linux container mode is faster but optional.
bottlenecks.diagnosis: The slow part is the network hop through Docker Desktop's published port, not files. The {{t:container|container run}} takes {{n:container}} against {{n:native_same_tree}} on Windows, and it is not the gate.
bottlenecks.firstStep: The container run becomes the gate. The Windows run triggers only when the Windows-side tools change. Expect one fix-up round for tests that depend on run order.
bottlenecks.proof: Median gate {{n:gate_target}}. Zero Linux-only failures on main.

ideas.adds: No idea touches how the check reaches its database. Your decision does.

bottlenecks.name: Checks queue behind each other
bottlenecks.said: Waits of 6 to 34 minutes. A second slot exists but opens only with 8 GB free.
bottlenecks.diagnosis: {{n:gib8}} was never free in {{n:samples}} samples (free memory ran from {{n:free_range}}), so there was one {{t:slot|slot}}. Waits ran from {{n:wait_min}} to {{n:wait_max}}. The longest came from releasing every parked session at once. The lock is not fair: a newcomer can jump a long waiter.
bottlenecks.firstStep: Measure one check's peak memory. Set the slots from that number. A fair queue with a printed position. One full gate per review round.
bottlenecks.proof: Second slot open on {{n:slot_target}} of the polls. Median wait {{n:wait_target}}.

ideas.adds: Two ideas add reruns to the queue. That is a conflict, settled by a rule, not a remedy.

bottlenecks.name: Memory is short
bottlenecks.said: Memory eaten by idle sessions and containers. Free memory often 2 to 6 GB.
bottlenecks.diagnosis: Idle sessions and containers are not shown to be the main holders. On a quiet reading the browser held {{n:mem_browser}}, the {{t:wsl|WSL2 machine}} {{n:mem_wsl}} and Claude {{n:mem_claude}}. {{n:dbs_stopped}} clinic databases are stopped.
bottlenecks.firstStep: One build day read from the always-on logger, by process group. Then choose among one shared test database, a cap on the WSL2 machine, and closing other applications.
bottlenecks.proof: A table of who holds memory when less than {{n:mem_low}} is free.

ideas.adds: The holders are a browser, a virtual machine and app processes. A logger names them.

bottlenecks.name: One check hung
bottlenecks.said: One Windows check hung for 600 seconds. Cause unknown, not reproduced.
bottlenecks.diagnosis: One Windows run stalled near the end of its tests with {{n:stall_free}} free. The watchdog killed it and the whole check took {{n:stall_run}}. The rerun passed. The hung test is unknown because the {{t:heartbeat|heartbeat}} carries no test name.
bottlenecks.firstStep: The heartbeat records the running test. On a stall, dump every worker's stack. Lower the stall limit from {{n:stall}} to {{n:stall_target}}, once {{n:falsekill}} on a loaded day show it kills no healthy check.
bottlenecks.proof: The next stall names its test and its kind of cause.

ideas.adds: No idea reaches the test runner. A heartbeat that names the running test does.

bottlenecks.name: Nothing restarts after a reboot
bottlenecks.said: After every restart Docker and the containers need a manual start.
bottlenecks.diagnosis: Docker Desktop's start-at-sign-in is off. {{n:containers_no}} containers have restart policy 'no'. Two settings, both known.
bottlenecks.firstStep: Docker starts at sign-in. Only the databases in use restart themselves, two at most until the power-offs are diagnosed. The check starts its own database when it is missing.
bottlenecks.proof: After a reboot and sign-in, the databases are healthy within {{n:db_target}} with no command.

ideas.adds: These are machine settings. Your yes switches them on.

bottlenecks.name: The work exists only on this PC
bottlenecks.said: No remote and no off-machine copy.
bottlenecks.diagnosis: No remote, by your choice. {{n:commits}} commits, {{n:worktrees}} worktrees and staged, uncommitted work sit on a PC that has powered off {{n:shutdowns}} times.
bottlenecks.firstStep: You pick custody: a private remote or an encrypted {{t:bundle|bundle}}. Then a bundle of every branch, verified, copied off the PC. A nightly copy that also captures uncommitted work.
bottlenecks.proof: A clone from the copy shows the same heads. The copy is under {{n:copy_age}} old.

ideas.adds: A custody decision and one git command. No idea is needed.

bottlenecks.name: Session reports overstate
bottlenecks.said: Records cited tests that did not exist and evidence that did not match. The orchestrator verifies everything itself.
bottlenecks.diagnosis: {{n:overstatements}} overstatements are on record: a record named two tests that no longer existed, '20 PASS' stood against 19 lines, a scan built nine checks while its record said 55.
bottlenecks.firstStep: Each slice commits a {{t:claims|claims file}}. A script checks that every cited test exists, ran, and fails when its guard is removed. It runs in the root's gate first. First replay it over the recorded gates.
bottlenecks.proof: The share of the {{n:overstatements}} recorded overstatements it flags. False flags {{n:false_flag}}.

ideas.adds: The script runs record-only, with an allow-list and no retry. A red test called 'pre-existing' is rerun at the commit before the fix.

bottlenecks.name: Shared documents have one writer
bottlenecks.said: The orchestrator applies every slice's edits. The board is over 800 lines and parts of the guides are stale.
bottlenecks.diagnosis: The board is {{n:board_kb}}. Its table rows run to thousands of characters. Only the root may edit the shared documents, so every slice's edits queue at the root.
bottlenecks.firstStep: Each slice writes a small {{t:fragment|state fragment}}. A generator builds a short board. The generated board's diff is a step of the local check. Tests compare the routing documents with the plan.
bottlenecks.proof: Board from {{n:board_kb}} to {{n:board_target}}. Root edits at merge: zero.

ideas.adds: The merge script applies the generated board diff. A transcript tally counts the root's edits at merge. The generator reports rows received, kept and dropped.

bottlenecks.name: You cannot see progress
bottlenecks.said: A session's step display did not move for an hour while it was working.
bottlenecks.diagnosis: Most likely one long foreground call, not a frozen display. A check may wait up to {{n:lock_bound}} for a slot before it even runs, and one {{n:foreground_loop}} foreground polling loop is on record.
bottlenecks.firstStep: The check writes a {{t:heartbeat|heartbeat}}: waiting with its place in the queue, running, or stalled. Checks run in the background, never in a foreground polling loop.
bottlenecks.proof: Longest gap between heartbeats {{n:heartbeat_gap}}.

ideas.adds: No kept idea is a progress signal. The heartbeat is. A live owner board fed by tool events would need hooks, so it is not in v2.

bottlenecks.name: Worktrees and containers pile up
bottlenecks.said: The orchestrator does not archive without the owner's word, after it once archived a session the owner was still using.
bottlenecks.diagnosis: {{n:worktrees}} worktrees and {{n:containers}} containers exist. The root archives nothing without your word. An app setting that would archive idle sessions is off.
bottlenecks.firstStep: A written archive rule. A reaper that only lists what it would remove: merged, clean worktrees and their containers. It skips anything written to in the last 24 hours and any worktree whose session is still open.
bottlenecks.proof: After each merge, worktree and container counts return to the active slices plus one.

ideas.adds: A clean-worktree check at merge, so the reaper meets no surprise. The archive rule stays yours.

bottlenecks.name: Reports flow through the orchestrator
bottlenecks.said: Subagents cannot write files. Their long reports come back through the orchestrator's context.
bottlenecks.diagnosis: Subagents can write files: a background subagent wrote and read back a file here, in a mode where nothing asks for permission. A read-only agent type, a tool list without Write, or an unanswered prompt would cause a refusal. Which of these hit the clinic is unknown. The rule came from two agents' unchecked report.
bottlenecks.firstStep: A 15-minute probe in the clinic's own permission mode. Then agents write the full report to a folder you have allowed and return a path, a hash and a short summary.
bottlenecks.proof: Refused writes: zero over {{n:writes20}} in the clinic's permission mode.

ideas.adds: A rule that would have stopped the false belief forming: check an environment fact with one command before it becomes a rule. It does not by itself move the refused-writes count.

bottlenecks.name: Nobody reads the final commit
bottlenecks.said: All review is model reading code. No independent human review.
bottlenecks.diagnosis: Executed proofs ran at every gate. The real gaps: no human reads anything, and the {{t:head|final head}} often merged with no independent read. {{n:unread_10nov}} merges on 10 November, and the real-data switch on 11 November, whose first root check then failed {{n:tests_failed}} tests. The 10 November merges followed your wrap-up instruction, so part of this was a decision.
bottlenecks.firstStep: A finding closes only on a test the harness runs. Each merge records who read the final head, and a {{t:highrisk|high-risk}} branch cannot merge on 'nobody' or 'its own session'. A replay of seven known misses with a fresh reviewer.
bottlenecks.proof: High-risk merges with an unread final head: from {{n:unread_hr}} to zero. The replay result is exploratory.

ideas.adds: Two ideas move the number. A merge whose verdict does not name the merged commit is refused. You read the changed lines the reviewer marks on high-risk merges. The rest make the merge record checkable against the transcript.

bottlenecks.name: Tests ran only on Windows
bottlenecks.said: Production is Linux. The Linux run is not the gate.
bottlenecks.diagnosis: The Linux container run exists since the last week of the build. It is faster and closer to production, and it is still optional.
bottlenecks.firstStep: The same decision as the slow check: the container run becomes the gate.
bottlenecks.proof: Median gate {{n:gate_target}}. Zero Linux-only failures on main.

ideas.adds: One decision answers this and the slow check together.

bottlenecks.name: Nothing has run on a real host
bottlenecks.said: Certificate, off-site backups, alerts and second-host restore are untested.
bottlenecks.diagnosis: Several items are unbuilt, not merely untested: no certificate script, nothing pushes backups off the host, no alert channel, no ssh hardening.
bottlenecks.firstStep: Free steps first, with you present for one administrator prompt: the fresh-machine restore, the first-deploy checklist end to end, an off-site push, an alert with a planted failure. Then a one-day rented host.
bottlenecks.proof: Each checklist gap has a result file from a real host.

ideas.adds: Each checklist step carries its command, its expected result and a run that must fail. A real host is still needed.

bottlenecks.name: The load test was not rerun
bottlenecks.said: Page speed is shown. 12 concurrent users is not.
bottlenecks.diagnosis: Page speed at volume was fixed and measured. The {{n:users12}} load run was not repeated after the query fix.
bottlenecks.firstStep: Rerun the load drill on current main. A bulk generator to reach {{n:moves250k}} stock movements. Rerun on the rented host.
bottlenecks.proof: A regression signal now. Proof of the real limits only on the host.

ideas.adds: Nothing about prompts or review reaches load testing. A rerun does.

bottlenecks.name: Minor findings pile up uncounted
bottlenecks.said: Dozens of P3 findings carried.
bottlenecks.diagnosis: Not dozens. {{n:p3_r1}} P3 findings in round one alone, and {{n:p3_board}} distinct P3 ids on the board with no status column. So no open count exists.
bottlenecks.firstStep: A script parses the board's finding tables into records: id, severity, status, closing commit, files. You set the rule for when a finding goes stale, and for a second look at anything on money, stock, access, import or restore.
bottlenecks.proof: An open count exists. Every pilot-critical finding has a verdict.

ideas.adds: One written scale and one status table, from which the parser is generated. An unknown status fails the parse, and dropped rows are counted.

phases.name: Keep the work safe, get back up
phases.oneLine: A copy off the PC, a restart that needs no commands, and a diagnosis of the power-offs.
phases.why: The PC powered off {{n:shutdowns}} times and the work exists only on it. Nothing else matters until that is covered. The idea lists add one small guard here and nothing else.

builds.name: Off-machine copy
builds.what: After your custody choice: a bundle of every branch, verified, copied off the PC. A nightly copy, run by a scheduled task, that also captures uncommitted work. The copy logs its own success, and the resume list warns when it is more than a day old. The November transcripts and the evidence folder go with it, because every later proof replays on them.

builds.name: Restart chain
builds.what: Docker starts at sign-in. The databases in use restart themselves, two at most until the power-offs are diagnosed. The check starts its own database if it is missing.

builds.name: Resume list
builds.what: At sign-in, a list of the sessions that were mid-work and where each branch stands. Sessions are released two at a time. A session whose record and branch disagree parks itself (mechanism 8).

builds.name: Shutdown diagnosis
builds.what: Join the 24 event times to commits and check logs. Your notes on mains outages. One always-on logger of temperature, power and memory by process group; phase 2 reads the same log. Decode the 7 October crash dump. No sleep while sessions hold work.

builds.name: Token baseline, saved early
builds.what: Rerun the token tally per slice on November's transcripts while they still exist. It costs no tokens. Phase 5 needs it, and the budget figure is set from it.

builds.name: One free rule from day one
builds.what: One fact, one command (mechanism 7): a fact about this PC or the tools is checked by a command before it becomes a rule. It costs a line in a brief.

proofs: A clone from the copy shows the same heads. The copy is under {{n:copy_age}} old.
After a reboot and sign-in, databases are healthy within {{n:db_target}} with no command.
The next unexpected shutdown has a trace that ends at it. Zero sleep-related events in {{n:sleep_target}}.
Idle time between 'could resume' and the next commit: from {{n:idle_days}} to {{n:idle_target}}.

cost.build: {{n:e_p1}} of one session. Scripts and settings only.
cost.owner: Five decisions now and two later. {{n:e_copy}} for the first copy, and {{n:e_sensor}} if you set up the sensor logger yourself. Your part comes after FixFlow's P0a.

phases.doneWhen: The copy is verified, one real reboot comes back with no command, and the logger is running.
phases.watch: The second check slot stays shut until the diagnosis names a cause that is not load, or {{n:load_days}} that include build load pass with no power-off.

phases.name: One fast check, sized by a measurement
phases.oneLine: The Linux container run becomes the gate. Slots are set from one measured number.
phases.why: The check is where the testbed's measured wins are: {{n:check_before}} came down to {{n:check_native}} when it ran in parallel. It is also where sessions wait. Every later phase runs through it, so it is fixed before anything is added to it.

builds.name: Container run as the gate
builds.what: The Linux container run becomes the gate. The Windows run triggers only when the Windows-side tools change. Expect one fix-up round for tests that depend on run order.

builds.name: Slots from one number
builds.what: Measure one check's peak memory. Set the slots from it. A fair queue that prints each check's place. One full gate per review round.

builds.name: Heartbeat
builds.what: The check writes waiting (with its place), running (with the current test) or stalled. Checks run in the background. On a stall every worker's stack is dumped. The stall limit comes down only after {{n:falsekill}} on a loaded day show it kills no healthy check.

builds.name: Memory table
builds.what: One build day read from phase 1's logger. A table of who holds memory when it is short. Then a choice among a shared test database, a cap on the WSL2 machine, and closing other applications.

builds.name: Clean-up
builds.what: A written archive rule. A reaper that lists merged, clean worktrees and their containers. It skips anything written to in the last 24 hours and any worktree whose session is still open.

proofs: Median gate {{n:gate_target}}. Zero Linux-only failures on main.
Second slot open on {{n:slot_target}} of the polls. Median wait {{n:wait_target}}.
Longest gap between heartbeats {{n:heartbeat_gap}}. The next stall names its test.
A table of who holds memory when less than {{n:mem_low}} is free.
After each merge, worktree and container counts return to the active slices plus one.

cost.build: {{n:e_p2}} of one session, including one observed build day for the memory table.
cost.owner: Two decisions now and one later, after the memory table exists.

phases.doneWhen: The container run is the gate, the peak-memory number is written down, and the heartbeat is live.
phases.watch: A second slot opens only if the measured peak allows it and phase 1's diagnosis does not point at load.

phases.name: Gate and review as scripts
phases.oneLine: Eleven mechanisms, scripts first. Each is accepted only by its own stated test, and for most that is a replay on the record.
phases.why: This is where the two idea lists land. They reach nothing for {{n:nothing}} of the 21 problems, which is why they could not come first. {{n:fit}} of the {{n:kept}} kept ideas fit a problem, and one dropped idea was promoted. All but one of those thirty reduce to eleven mechanisms. The testbed had already practised {{n:practised}} of the dropped ideas: {{n:worked33}} worked and {{n:failed38}} failed, mostly as lines in a brief and model re-checks. So v2 takes them as scripts that can fail.

builds.name: Reports on disk
builds.what: After a 15-minute write probe: agents write full reports to a folder you have allowed and hand back a path, a hash and a short summary.

builds.name: Generated board
builds.what: Each slice writes a small state fragment. A generator builds a short board. The root stops editing it by hand.

builds.name: Six scripts that spend no tokens
builds.what: Sealed replay, verdict script, transcript audit, finding table, dry run with stand-in agents, merge queue. In that order.

builds.name: Gate workflow
builds.what: First a probe that a workflow agent can run the check at all. Then the round's reviewers run in a saved workflow outside the root, write their reports to disk and return the typed verdict. It is tested with stand-in agents before any real one.

builds.name: Touch-list test
builds.what: At zero tokens, on the ten recorded cases: does the file of the later defect fall inside the list? The list is dropped if {{n:blast_drop}} do, or if it runs past {{n:blast_files}}.

builds.name: Index replay
builds.what: At zero tokens, on the recorded windows: build an import-and-caller index at each window's start commit, count the lookup-only calls it would have answered, and check whether its list holds the files the window went on to edit. An index earns a live trial only if this says so. It reads the clinic repository and the transcripts and writes nothing there.

builds.name: The fix-round contract
builds.what: The contract and its clauses (mechanism 9), replayed under the seal on the recorded chains before any live use.

builds.name: Two things that cost people or tokens, last
builds.what: You read the marked lines of three high-risk merges. A short tool list for gate agents, after a with-and-without test.

proofs: Each mechanism passes its own stated test. See the ladder below.
High-risk merges with an unread final head: from {{n:unread_hr}} to zero.
Board from {{n:board_kb}} to {{n:board_target}}. Root edits at merge: zero.
The claims script flags the recorded overstatements with false flags {{n:false_flag}}.
An open count exists over the {{n:p3_board}} P3 ids.
No compaction of the root across a wave of {{n:wave5}}.

cost.build: {{n:e_p3}} of one session for the scripts.
cost.agents: While it is being built: replays and probes only, outside build hours, two at a time. Once it is live: each fix round adds at most one fresh reviewer, and a high-risk merge whose branch changed adds one read.
cost.owner: Decisions as each mechanism reaches you. {{n:replay_owner}} of reading across the review replay and the three-merge trial.

phases.doneWhen: Each of the six scripts has passed its stated test, and the merge queue has run record-only over the {{n:merges}} recorded merges.
phases.watch: A script may refuse a merge only after you say so.

phases.name: First use and a real host
phases.oneLine: A clean-install walk in every gate, and one rehearsal on a real machine.
phases.why: The last-day gaps were missing production paths hidden behind test data. Only walking a clean install finds them. The walk runs inside the container gate, so it needs phase 2.

builds.name: Zero-seed walk in every gate
builds.what: Against a fresh container database: install, first user, tills and accounts, a real-shaped import, one transaction, close of day. Plus a test that every kind of record the seeder writes can also be created in production.

builds.name: Real-host rehearsal
builds.what: Free steps first, with you present for one administrator prompt: fresh-machine restore, the first-deploy checklist, an off-site push, an alert with a planted failure. Each step has its command, its expected result and a run that must fail. Then a rented host for a day, with made-up data only.

builds.name: Load rerun
builds.what: Rerun the {{n:users12}} drill on current main. A bulk generator to reach {{n:moves250k}} stock movements. Rerun on the rented host.

proofs: The walk fails on the commit before the 11 November merge and passes after it.
Each first-deploy gap has a result file from a real host.
A regression signal from the load rerun now. Proof of the real limits only on the host.

cost.build: {{n:e_p4}} of one session, including the work to close the rig's gaps.
cost.agents: None. The walk adds {{n:zero_seed_run}} to every gate run.
cost.owner: One decision. {{n:e_uac}} for the administrator prompt. {{n:e_host}}.

phases.doneWhen: The walk is a gate step and has caught the 11 November gap on replay. The checklist has run once on a real host.
phases.watch: Rig steps need an administrator prompt, so they cannot run while you are away.

phases.name: One token budget
phases.oneLine: Measure where tokens go per slice, tune the one budget, and try the weak compaction-window trial.
phases.why: The three-day stop was a power-off. Usage limits did interrupt work on other days, and how much is not measured. Nobody knows how {{t:reread|re-read tokens}} count against the plan's limit, so no token cut can promise fewer stops. That is why this is last.

builds.name: The budget as numbers
builds.what: Per-slice tokens and limit events for November, from the baseline saved in phase 1. The budget figure set in phase 1 is checked against them.

builds.name: Lever 1: slice sessions
builds.what: The largest share: {{n:slice_share}} of tokens. One phase per session. A smaller mandatory pre-read. The compaction-window trial. What an index could touch there is estimated as two exposures, which overlap: {{n:fill_fetched}} of context is content the sessions fetched by reading, and calls that only read or search re-read {{n:step_tokens}} of all tokens. Neither is a saving. The index replay in phase 3 is the first test.

builds.name: Lever 2: fixed cost per agent
builds.what: {{n:fixed_cost}} before any work. Fewer connectors and skills in agent sessions. Fewer tiny fan-outs. The short tool list from phase 3.

builds.name: Lever 3: the root
builds.what: The gate workflow and merge queue from phase 3. Bounded: the root is {{n:root_share}} of tokens.

builds.name: The compaction-window trial
builds.what: {{n:over400}} of November's tokens were in calls whose context had passed 400k. That is {{t:exposure|exposure}}, not a saving. Phase 1's baseline narrows it: sessions on Opus never passed {{n:opus_max}} and compacted there {{n:comp_367}} times, while sessions on Sonnet ran to {{n:sonnet_max}}. So the calls above 400k are on Sonnet and Fable. The trial: set the window to {{n:window}} for Sonnet slice sessions, for one wave. Confirm it took effect: compactions should show near {{n:trigger}}. Charge each compaction call to the trial. Check one summary against the slice's task record. The result will be an anecdote.

proofs: Per-slice token figures exist for November.
The trial shows compactions near {{n:trigger}}, with their cost counted on the trial's side.
No promise is made that fewer tokens means fewer stops. That link is unknown.

cost.build: {{n:e_p5}} for the tally. The trial is a setting.
cost.agents: None extra. Each extra compaction pays for one full-context call.

phases.doneWhen: The per-slice baseline exists and the budget is checked against it. The trial is optional.
phases.watch: The budget rule itself applies from phase 1. This phase only measures and tunes it.

deps.label: Find out why the PC powers off before adding load. The second slot waits for that.
Replays and verdict scripts take check time. They want one fast gate first.
The first-use walk runs inside the container gate.
The gate workflow and tool list change what a session costs. Measure after.
The token baseline is saved in phase 1, while the transcripts still exist.

order.kept: The five phases stay in the order given.
changes: The budget rule (two lanes, a written budget per window) applies from phase 1, and its figure is set in phase 1. Phase 5 measures and tunes it. Reason: the refuter warned that the remedies added together recreate the stops.
The token baseline is saved in phase 1. Reason: it needs the November transcripts, and the app may clean them up.
Mechanisms 7 and 8 enter in phase 1. Reason: they cost a line in a brief, and the resume check guards the resume list that phase 1 builds.
Inside phase 3 the scripts come before the fix-round contract. The compile's first list of moves had the contract first. Reason: the contract's replay needs the seal and the verdict script.

Phase 4 needs only phase 2. It can swap with phase 3 if you want the clean-install walk sooner. It sits fourth because it draws on check minutes, on the rig's memory and on your presence for an administrator prompt.

rules.name: The ship plan comes first
rules.text: FixFlow's P0a is the next session and nothing here delays or edits it. Your part of phase 1 comes after P0a. Harness work takes neither the Docker gate nor agent lanes while a FixFlow phase is running or waiting on its reviewer: both draw on the same usage limit.

rules.name: One budget
rules.text: Lanes two at a time. A token budget written down before any launch. One agent-adding change per window. State on disk.

rules.name: Script before agent
rules.text: Models find things. Scripts decide whether a finding is closed. A check a script can make is never left to a model.

rules.name: Replay before live
rules.text: A gate-and-review mechanism is accepted by its replay on the record wherever a replay is possible. It runs record-only before it may refuse anything.

rules.name: One fact, one command
rules.text: A fact about this PC or the tools becomes a rule only after one command has checked it. The original list carried five facts that turned out wrong.

rules.name: Your yes for anything that reaches outside
rules.text: No hooks, no installs, no scheduled tasks, no permission changes and nothing leaving this PC without your decision.

mechanisms.name: Sealed replay
mechanisms.plain: A replay that cannot peek at the answer.
mechanisms.what: The replay runs in a clone with no later commits. The answer key is hashed first and committed only after judging. A read log from the replay agent's transcript shows what it opened. Both arms read the same commit and the same brief, or the result is marked not comparable.
mechanisms.replay: Run one recorded fix chain in a sealed clone and in a plain worktree. The read log must show zero opens of the later fix, the finding tables or the board.

mechanisms.name: Verdict script for each gate round
mechanisms.plain: A script checks every claim a round makes and writes a small fixed-format verdict.
mechanisms.what: Only an assertion failure counts as fail-before. Tests before and after the fix are compared for weakened expectations. A red test called 'pre-existing' is rerun at the commit before the fix. A search of the diff lists any test switched off and any check setting changed. It runs record-only, with no retry and an allow-list. Lines nobody ran are marked 'read, not run'. The verdict names the commit. One open point: a flaky test can fail that rerun for the wrong reason, and the rule for that is not written yet.
mechanisms.costText: A script, plus check-slot time for the cited tests.
mechanisms.replay: For each closed P1 that cites a test, run it at the fix's parent: count assertion failures against collection errors. Score the {{n:overstatements}} recorded overstatements. False flags {{n:false_flag}}.

mechanisms.name: Transcript audit at merge
mechanisms.plain: The tool's own records say who read what. A script compares that with what the merge record claims.
mechanisms.what: A self-reported merge record can be filled in falsely. The transcript is an independent source: did a reviewer read the final head, did the gate run before each fix commit, how many root edits touched shared files. It records and blocks nothing. No hook.
mechanisms.replay: Run it over the 10 and 11 November merges. It must find the unread final heads by itself and give a root-edit count per merge.

mechanisms.name: One finding table
mechanisms.plain: Severity and status words are written once. The parser is generated from them. Every row is counted.
mechanisms.what: P0 to P3 and every status are defined in one table. The parser's allowed values come from that table, so an unknown status fails the parse. Rows received, kept and dropped are reported, and no open count is given while a drop is unexplained.
mechanisms.replay: Parse the board: zero unmapped statuses, every dropped row explained, an open count over the {{n:p3_board}} P3 ids.

mechanisms.name: Dry run with stand-in agents
mechanisms.plain: The new gate and merge scripts are run with fake agents that fail in every way.
mechanisms.what: The scripts run with stand-in agents that return nothing, crash, or disagree. A dead reviewer must never read as a clean one.
mechanisms.replay: Planted cases only, because the testbed had no gate script: a reviewer that returns nothing, a crash, a refuted verdict, a reader of 'nobody' on a high-risk branch. None may reach merge.

mechanisms.name: Merge queue that checks the commit
mechanisms.plain: A script merges under a lock, and only when the verdict names the exact commit being merged.
mechanisms.what: It merges under a lock, runs the check on the merged result, applies the generated board diff and flags a dirty worktree. It starts record-only: it is replayed over the recorded merges before it may refuse anything.
mechanisms.replay: Record-only over the {{n:merges}} recorded merges, it must flag the unread heads of 10 and 11 November. Live: unread high-risk final heads from {{n:unread_hr}} to zero.

mechanisms.name: One fact, one command
mechanisms.plain: A fact about the PC or the tools becomes a rule only after one command checks it.
mechanisms.what: A fact reported by an agent or stated by anyone is checked by one command before it becomes a harness rule. Each first-deploy step carries a command, an expected result and a run that must fail.
mechanisms.costText: A line in a brief. Free.
mechanisms.replay: Count the environment facts in the root's {{n:lessons}} lessons and the 21 problem statements that one command could check, and how many turned out wrong. This is a baseline. It passes or fails nothing.
mechanisms.accepted: a baseline count, not a pass or fail

mechanisms.name: Resume check
mechanisms.plain: A released session compares its record with its branch. A mismatch parks it.
mechanisms.what: After many power-offs a session's record and its branch can drift apart. A session whose branch holds commits its record does not cover lists them and stops. A matching record resumes with no wait.
mechanisms.costText: A line in a brief. Free.

fix.shows: Left: one recorded chain, the cutoff guards, step by step. Right: the clause of the fix-round contract that would apply at that step.

steps.today: Two reviewers find a blocking defect: a same-day import is counted twice.
steps.clause: A finding blocks only if it states a failing condition.
steps.detail: That condition becomes a test before anyone writes a fix.

steps.today: The fix: treat a stock opening as the shelf at the end of its cutoff day.
steps.clause: The test must fail before the fix and pass after it.
steps.detail: A script checks both, and only a real assertion failure counts.

steps.today: The slice's own re-review finds the fix made three new serious defects.
steps.clause: The full gate runs before the fix commit. If it is red: revert.

steps.today: The fix for one of them adds a hold on a batch's medicines until the batch posts. The hold is new stored state.
steps.clause: New stored state gets a table: every way it ends, and a test for each.
steps.detail: With hindsight, two rows of that table are the next two defects. Whether a table written at the time would have listed them is exactly what the replay tests.

steps.today: The hold never ends. An abandoned batch leaves its medicines refused for good.
steps.clause: A fresh reviewer re-reads, with a list of what the fix touches.
steps.detail: Not the reviewer from round one.

steps.today: The next fix starts the hold earlier. Now a stuck batch holds its medicines for good once its preparer has left.
steps.clause: Two rounds at most. A finding that fails twice goes to a fresh agent on a fresh brief.
steps.detail: A third failure goes back to planning, not to another patch.

steps.today: Another re-review finds a real wrong figure. It is fixed, and the root reads that last diff alone. The gate passes at round three.
steps.detail: The verdict script writes what was run and what was only read.

fix.todayResult: One defect became a chain of fixes. Chains like this are on record for three branches. Across the build, {{n:rounds3}} gates took three rounds, and fixes created {{n:p1_fix}} new P1s.
fix.contractResult: This is a trial. Nobody has measured whether the contract lowers the number of defects that fixes create. Its first test is a sealed replay on these recorded chains.
assume: The left side is from the record. The right side is a design and has never been run.
The demo pairs each recorded step with a clause. It does not show the clause catching the defect.
The replay asks one question: would the table and the touch list have demanded the tests the five late P1s needed?

Record-only comes first: the queue is replayed over the {{n:merges}} recorded merges before it may refuse anything.
Refusing is your decision. This design proposes that your recorded word can lift one refusal, and the record then says the head went in unread.
The high-risk list is a proposal. The testbed never named one.

tokens.name: Where the tokens went
tokens.shows: November's {{n:total_tokens}} cache-read tokens, by kind of session and by how large the context was on each call.

views.label: By session
views.text: Slice sessions took {{n:slice_share}}. The root, which the list blamed, took {{n:root_share}}.

views.label: By call size
views.text: Each bar is split by how much context the call carried. Large calls dominate the slice sessions and the root.

views.label: The 400k line
views.text: {{n:over400}} of the tokens were in calls whose context had passed 400k: {{n:over400_slice}} in slice sessions, {{n:over400_root}} in the root. The context above the line in those calls adds up to {{n:above_line}} tokens, equal to {{n:above_line_pct}} of the total.

tokens.caution: This is exposure, not a saving. A compacted session drops far below the line, so later calls shrink by more than the part above it. But each extra compaction pays for a full-context summary call, a cache rewrite and re-reads. Nobody has measured either effect here.

sketch.title: What a compaction window does to one session
sketch.text: A sketch, not data. Context grows with every call until a compaction cuts it. On a model with a one-million window the root compacted at {{n:native_trigger}}. A {{n:window}} window triggers at {{n:trigger}}. How far the context drops, and what each cut costs, are not measured here.
sketch.against: Against it on record: in one vendor's benchmark, compacting first scored lower than keeping the full history. It was three runs and cannot be repeated here.

assume: The bars are measured. The sketch below them is illustrative.
What the windows hold, and what an index could touch, is shown on the architecture page.
Shares are of cache-read tokens, which were nearly all of the tokens.
Sessions on Opus already compact near 367k, because of that model's own window: {{n:comp_367}} of the {{n:comp_total}} compactions on record. The calls above 400k are on Sonnet and Fable.
That is a comparison across models, not a trial: the two groups did different work.
Nobody has traced whether that setting reaches sessions in the desktop app.
No trial here has compared two window sizes.
A token cut may not prevent a single stop: the three-day stop was a power-off.

root.name: The root as the only gate
root.shows: Five slices finish. Left: every review, merge and board edit passes through the root. Right: a gate workflow and a merge queue do the mechanical part.

steps: Briefs two reviewers; their reports come back into its context
Reads the last fix diff itself
Edits the board and shared documents
The gate workflow runs the reviewers; reports go to disk
A typed verdict comes back: the commit read, pass or fail per finding
The merge queue merges under a lock and tests the result
The board is generated; the root edits nothing
The root judges what the scripts cannot

root.fillNote: The fill levels are illustrative. Measured: the root compacted {{n:compactions}} times, at {{n:compaction_sizes}}, and its calls averaged {{n:root_ctx}} tokens of context. The only per-gate figure on record is a rough one: {{n:root_per_gate}} tokens of root reading per gate.
root.bound: The gain is bounded. The root is {{n:root_share}} of November's tokens. This removes a bottleneck. It is not the big token saving.
assume: How much each gate adds to the root's context is not measured. The two step sizes are made up to show the difference in kind.
The target is no compaction across a wave of {{n:wave5}}. It is a trial.
Whether a workflow agent can run the check at all needs one probe first.
Gate workflows run two agents at a time at most, inside the one budget.
Merges still happen one at a time. A script holding a lock does them, not a session holding everything in its head.
